trust_decision.summary: Whether the tx signer (proto signer field) controls the DID a message acts as. At the pinned commit only the IID ante decides this, for top-level IidTxMsgs only. Keeper handlers spend funds or mutate state for a DID-resolved address or a DID-equality match without re-binding it to the signer, so routes that skip the ante (authz MsgExec inner msgs, CosmWasm-dispatched msgs, ICA host with allow-all) are unchecked.

landing_point.why: The summary names an 'x/bonds DID-resolved payer drain'. MakeOutcomePayment resolves SenderDid's fragment to an address (line 698) and deposits from it (line 715) without comparing it to SenderAddress.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The ante already checks signer-vs-DID for IidTxMsgs, and authz itself requires the grantee to hold a grant from the granter. ICA/wasm dispatch is 'by design' and set in an old v4 upgrade handler, so a solver patching bonds handlers can argue the wrapper and transport routes are a neighbouring feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Authz-delegated claims. In MsgSubmitClaim/MsgEvaluateClaim the signer is the collection admin, while AgentDid names a different party and is attribution only. A blanket 'signer must control every *_did' rule breaks delegated submission and evaluation. The fix removed these from IidTxMsg for that reason. Also, the IID ante accepts the AssertionMethod relationship as well as Authentication. A legitimate MsgExec with an authorized granter must also keep passing.

message dispatched without ante (wasm / ICA host / router direct)
DID fragment whose verification method resolves to an address other than the signer

O8_uncovered_routes.route: MsgCreateEntity: OwnerDid is written as a controller of the new entity DID with no in-keeper signer-to-OwnerDid binding. The fix added the keeper check to the other three entity handlers but not this one.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Create only makes a new entity; no existing victim state is mutated, so 'acting as' another DID looks harmless.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as three fixed sites

O8_uncovered_routes.route: MsgDisputeClaim: DisputerDid is recorded from AgentDid, and the keeper relies on the IID ante for the signer-to-AgentDid binding (comment says so).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Comment says the ante validates it, the fix's own comments say MsgDisputeClaim correctly stays IidTxMsg, and the field is attribution only.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: MsgClaimIntent: still an IidTxMsg via GetIidController; the keeper stores AgentDid on the intent without binding it to AgentAddress.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Authorization is the authz SubmitClaimAuthorization grant check (lines 959-966), so AgentDid looks like attribution only.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Bonds DID-equality gates (EditBond CreatorDid==EditorDid, UpdateBondState ControllerDid==EditorDid, SetNextAlpha OracleDid, WithdrawReserve ControllerDid==WithdrawerDid) never bind signer to DID in-keeper. The published fix closed them only by disabling the module.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The report leads to payer-drain handlers (Buy/Sell/MakeOutcomePayment); DID-equality gates look like they already 'check authorization'.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An entity-account handler that resolves the owner via a DID instead of CheckIfOwner on OwnerAddress.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same file mixes DID-based and address-based owner checks; a maintainer adding a DID-keyed variant would copy the UpdateEntity pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Batch end-blocker re-resolves the stored order's AccountDid fragment to an address at execution time (save/reload of a DID reference).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The order stores only the DID fragment (msg_server.go:476), so re-resolving at batch time is the natural implementation; a check at message time does not cover it.

O9_family: missing authorization / confused deputy: authorization is enforced only in the tx ante, and keeper handlers act for a DID-resolved principal on routes that skip the ante (CWE-862/CWE-285)

unverified: The published fix neutralises bonds with a kill switch (disabled msg server, no-op EndBlocker, ante reject) rather than a signer check. Hidden tests asserting ErrBondsModuleDisabled would be unfair; graders would need rewriting as behavioural 'unauthorized signer rejected, authorized passes' tests. This is the main task-design risk but not a listed red-flag enum.
The ICA allow-list part of the fix is a state migration in a new upgrade handler; it is hard to test behaviourally without an IBC harness, and a solver would not naturally add an upgrade.
